title: PCcheck: Persistent Concurrent Checkpointing for ML
problem: Checkpointing large ML training runs to persistent storage introduces high overhead when done at high frequency, yet infrequent checkpointing leads to long recovery times after failures — a growing problem as training scale increases and cheap spot VMs dramatically raise failure rates.
motivation: As ML training jobs scale to thousands of GPUs over weeks and increasingly use preemptible spot VMs, the probability and cost of failures rises sharply, requiring checkpointing solutions that are simultaneously low-overhead and high-frequency.
method: PCcheck saves neural network models to durable storage while training continues, by overlapping the storage I/O with GPU computation so neither blocks the other. It uses copy-on-write snapshots (capturing only what changes in model state) and pipelined multi-stage I/O (sending data to storage in stages). The system tracks consistency across concurrent training steps to guarantee each checkpoint is valid and recoverable.
key_novelty: PCcheck overlaps checkpoint storage with training compute using copy-on-write snapshots and pipelined I/O, enabling frequent durable checkpoints without slowing training.
contributions: PCcheck: a persistent concurrent checkpointing system for large-scale ML training
Copy-on-write model state snapshots enabling overlap of checkpoint I/O with training computation
Pipelined multi-stage I/O reducing checkpoint-induced training pauses
Support for high-frequency checkpointing with low overhead on spot VMs and large GPU clusters
